findings.title: No File > Open Recent; recents vanish once a dataset is open
findings.what: The File commands (CommandGroup replacing .newItem, lines 144-171) hold New Dataset Window, Open Dataset… and a conditional 'Reopen <last>' only. Recents appear only on WelcomeWorkspace (WorkspaceView.swift ~line 515, prefix(5)), which is shown only while no document is open. Nothing in DatasetCommands reads `recents`, and `AppState.openRecent` already exists (App/AppState+DatasetSession.swift:11). Once a dataset is loaded, the only way back to another one is the file picker.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Keyboards: respect the standard shortcuts, with Command-O as 'display a dialog for choosing a document to open'. A Mac user also expects Open Recent beside it, but I could not retrieve a menu-bar HIG page on this server, so that part is convention, not a quoted rule.
findings.fix: Add a `Menu("Open Recent")` under Open Dataset… listing `recents.entries` (display name plus the disambiguating location), with a Clear Menu item. Pass `recents` into DatasetCommands and call `perform(.openRecent)` or `appState.openRecent`. Disable the items while loading, as Open is.

findings.title: Dropping a file on the window or Dock icon does nothing
findings.what: DatasetWindow handles only `.onOpenURL` (Finder Open With). A grep for dropDestination, onDrop and NSDocumentController finds nothing in UI/ or App/. A dataset dragged onto the window or the Welcome screen is ignored.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Keyboards: Full Keyboard Access is meant to allow 'drag and drop' style interactions, and drag and drop is a core Mac gesture for opening files. Convention, not a quoted rule.
findings.fix: Add `.dropDestination(for: URL.self)` on ContentView or the window root, calling `appState.openFile(url:)` for the first URL. Respect the same loading and busy guard as Open Dataset…. Pure SwiftUI.

findings.title: Toolbar actions Reveal in Finder and Open with Options… have no menu-bar command
findings.what: The toolbar has Reveal in Finder (WorkspaceView.swift:226-239) and the Dataset menu offers Open with Options… (WorkspaceView.swift:204). DatasetCommands has no Reveal command and no Open with Options… item. Open with Options is also on the Welcome screen and in the sidebar, but only as buttons. The toolbar's Preprocess and Export Diffraction PNG do have menu equivalents.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Toolbars (macOS): 'Make every toolbar item available as a command in the menu bar', because the toolbar can be hidden or overflowed. Here Reveal sits at `.visibilityPriority(.low)` and goes into the overflow first.
findings.fix: Add 'Open with Options…' (for example Option-Command-O) next to Open Dataset…, and 'Show in Finder' (Shift-Command-R, say) to the Dataset menu, disabled without a dataset.

findings.title: Warnings are whole sentences in orange or red text, against the owner's recipe
findings.what: RequirementsSection puts `.foregroundStyle(.orange)` on the whole Label, so the title text is orange (225-227). Other inspector text is coloured the same way: the promote-run halt in `.red` (~826), the rotation refusal in `.orange` (~881), and the replay refusal in `.orange` (~1026). The sidebar's `warning(...)` Label headline is orange the same way (WorkspaceSidebar.swift ~346). Rotation-curve explanations are `.caption2` in `.tertiary`.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Accessibility (colour and contrast), plus the owner recipe in inspector-hig-recipe: text in system label colours, colour on status symbols only. System orange caption text on a light background is low contrast.
findings.fix: Use `Label { Text(...) } icon: { Image(...).foregroundStyle(.orange) }` so only the glyph is coloured and the sentence stays `.primary` or `.secondary`. Do the same for the red and orange `Text` lines, with a warning-triangle glyph prefix. Raise the rotation caption from tertiary to secondary. A text-colour fix is not a structure or width change, but confirm with the owner because the file is frozen. The sidebar half is not frozen and can go first.

findings.title: Shortcuts: inspector has a hidden second key and a Control-modifier one; no Command-. for Cancel
findings.what: The menu item 'Show/Hide Inspector' uses Control-Command-I (198-201). The toolbar button carries a different, undocumented Option-Command-0 (WorkspaceInspector.swift:161). Run is Command-R in the menu (212) and a hidden Command-Return on the toolbar button (WorkspaceView.swift:282). Cancel Analysis is Esc only (216); the toolbar and status-strip Cancel buttons have no shortcut. Tools and Bottom Pane also use Control-Command (S and L).
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Keyboards: Command-Period is 'Cancel an operation'; Option-Command-I is 'Display an inspector window'; 'Avoid using the Control key as a modifier'; Command is the preferred main modifier. Esc as 'cancel the current action' is also listed, so keeping Esc is fine. Control-Command-S for the sidebar is the system's own and should stay.
findings.fix: Make the menu item and the button agree on one visible shortcut. Option-Command-I is the HIG choice; Option-Command-0 is the owner's Xcode reference. Drop the extra hidden keys, or list them in the menu. Add Command-Period to Cancel Analysis, and consider replacing Control-Command-L. The menu change is in mac4DSTEMApp.swift, which is not frozen. The inspector button's shortcut is in a frozen file, so removing it needs the owner's accepted picture.

findings.title: Toolbar trailing group has a text-labelled verb touching icon-only buttons with no spacer
findings.what: The four `.primaryAction` items (PrimaryActionButton, SaveResultButton, RevealDatasetButton, DatasetMenu) are adjacent. The verb is a text button ('Compute Image', 'Detect All Disks', 'Calibrate Origin'). The other three are icon-only. The only spacer is the flexible one before the group (line 240).
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Toolbars: 'Keep actions with text labels separate' because a text action next to a symbol can read as one combined control; 'insert fixed space'. The same page recommends at most three groups and putting the primary action on the trailing side.
findings.fix: Insert `ToolbarSpacer(.fixed, placement: .primaryAction)` between the verb and the utility group (Save, Reveal, Dataset). This also keeps the prominent glass button from sharing a capsule with the others. Inspector toggle is already separate. I have not seen it on screen, so confirm against a screenshot first.

findings.title: Pane and process-area dividers cannot be operated by keyboard or VoiceOver
findings.what: PaneSplit's divider is a `Divider` with a DragGesture and the label 'Resize the diffraction and real-space panes', and the status strip is dragged by a simultaneous DragGesture (737). Neither has `accessibilityAdjustableAction` or any key handler. The label promises an operable control that does nothing for VoiceOver. Bottom-pane show/hide has a menu command, but sizing does not.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Keyboards: support Full Keyboard Access; Accessibility: do not make gestures the only way. Other custom controls in this app already offer adjustable actions (ImagePanes.swift:493, SpectrumStripView.swift:92).
findings.fix: Add `.accessibilityAdjustableAction` on both dividers (increment and decrement move the fraction a step) with an `accessibilityValue` such as '50 percent'. Optionally double-click the divider to centre it, which is standard on the Mac. No visual change.

findings.title: Settings window always opens on General
findings.what: `@State private var selection: SettingsSection? = .general`. Reopening Settings, or the window being rebuilt, goes back to General, whichever pane was last used.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Settings (macOS): 'Restore the most recently viewed pane'; 'Update the window's title to reflect the currently visible pane' (already done via navigationTitle). The sidebar form itself is the owner's choice (ROADMAP 'Xcode-style sidebar'); the HIG's toolbar-tab style is not recommended here against that decision.
findings.fix: Store the selection with `@AppStorage` or `@SceneStorage` keyed by the section raw value, with a fallback to General.

findings.title: Welcome screen carries marketing copy the owner has already ruled out
findings.what: WelcomeWorkspace shows a largeTitle 'Turn 4D-STEM data into answers' and a title3 'A native Mac workspace for calibrated imaging, quantitative maps, and phase reconstruction.' The file's own comment says the old brochure cards were removed as filler.
findings.guideline: Owner rule in CLAUDE.md: 'No filler: every control, number and sentence earns its place or goes'. Human Interface Guidelines, Writing: be direct.
findings.fix: Replace the two lines with the app name and the actions. The window needs only the doors and the local-disk note. This is a wording and structure change in a frozen file, so it needs an accepted picture. It does not correct a false claim, so the ADR 050 wording exception does not apply.

findings.title: Sidebar hints are one-line truncated with the full text on hover only
findings.what: The next-step hint (a `.caption` Text) and the session explainer 'Loaded with the dataset — from earlier analysis' (`.caption2`, `lineLimit(1)`) take a one-line ideal and truncate. The file's comments say the full text is on `.help`. The workflow guidance and the 'not computed in this session' provenance are therefore unreadable in the narrowest sidebar, and hover is not reachable by keyboard or VoiceOver.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Accessibility: do not hide essential information behind a pointer-only affordance. Owner rule: nothing truncated.
findings.fix: Allow these two texts to wrap (`.lineLimit(nil)` or 3, with `fixedSize(horizontal: false, vertical: true)`) and add `.accessibilityHint`/`.accessibilityLabel` with the full sentence. The comment says a fixedSize caused a split-column minimum problem, so check on screen first.

findings.title: Same action named differently in menu and toolbar: 'Export Diffraction Pattern…' vs 'Export Diffraction PNG…'
findings.what: The Dataset toolbar menu says 'Export Diffraction PNG…' (WorkspaceView.swift:213). The File menu item that calls `exportDiffractionImage()` says 'Export Diffraction Pattern…' (mac4DSTEMApp.swift:177). The toolbar's wording also names a format the sheet may no longer be limited to.
findings.guideline: Human Interface Guidelines, Toolbars (macOS): toolbar items should be menu commands; use one name for one command so people can find it in both places.
findings.fix: Use one title, preferably 'Export Diffraction Pattern…', in both places. Check against the figure-export lane's current wording before editing, since that lane is working on export code now.

notChecked: Nothing was run or seen on screen. Everything is from reading code and the Apple documentation server. HIG pages retrieved and relied on: Keyboards, Toolbars, Settings, Context menus. findings.title: Diffraction pane has no pointer readout (qx, qy, value) while placing apertures or choosing fit radii
findings.what: The only onContinuousHover in the panes file is the real-space pane (line 1108, feeding CursorReadout). DiffractionPane (lines ~30-455) has none, so hovering the pattern shows no detector pixel or intensity. Detector coordinates the user must reason in (aperture centre/radii, 'Fit annulus inner/outer' px in PrepareSettings, ring positions) cannot be read off the pattern. Aperture numbers exist only as read-only rows in the Info tab (WorkspaceInspector apertureSection, line ~446), not in Imaging's Settings tab.
findings.guideline: HIG Sliders: 'Consider supplementing a slider with a corresponding text field' and show exact values; HIG Keyboards: arrow keys move a selected item by the smallest app unit. Cursor feedback is the basic precision aid for drag placement.
findings.fix: Add the same hover readout the real-space pane has to the diffraction header: 'x 64, y 60 · 1.2e3', in detector pixels (plus calibrated q when set). Reuse CursorSampleModel; no new layout since the header already has a trailing slot.

findings.title: Aperture placement is drag-only; no numeric entry or keyboard nudge in the Imaging inspector
findings.what: Imaging Settings offers shape, BF/ADF/HAADF presets and a note 'Drag the detector on the diffraction pane'. Centre and radii appear only as read-only InspectorValueRows in the Info tab (WorkspaceInspector.swift:446, frozen). ApertureOverlay snaps to whole pixels (emit -> snappedEdit, PaneOverlays.swift ~817), which helps, but there is no typed centre/radius and the handles (12 pt) are not keyboard focusable; Slider twins exist only inside accessibilityRepresentation (PaneOverlays.swift ~661), reachable by VoiceOver but not by Tab or arrow keys. Region mode does have a Radius AdjustmentSlider (with field), so the two directions are inconsistent.
findings.guideline: HIG Sliders ('text field and stepper for exact values'); HIG Keyboards ('holding an arrow key moves the selected item by the smallest app-defined unit'; Shift constrains while dragging).
findings.fix: Add inspector rows to the Detector section: Center X, Center Y, Inner r, Outer r as NumericField + stepper (integers, same snappedEdit/commit path), shown only for relevant shapes. Optionally let a focused aperture take arrow-key nudges. Not a conflict with owner rules: it is one more row group in a non-frozen room view, and the Info rows could then be dropped (net fewer numbers).

findings.title: Zoom is about the pane centre, with no scroll-wheel, keyboard or menu route
findings.what: zoomPan() attaches MagnifyGesture plus DragGesture plus double-tap reset. The image is scaled by scaleEffect about its centre (header comment lines 12-16), so pinching never keeps the point under the cursor fixed; the user must zoom, then pan back. The header comment (lines 5-10) says macOS synthesises magnification from a mouse wheel; that only holds with the system's Accessibility zoom option, not by default. App/mac4DSTEMApp.swift defines no View-menu Zoom In / Zoom Out / Actual Size; the only non-gesture route is the VoiceOver action list (lines 178-190). Mouse and keyboard-only users cannot zoom a pattern.
findings.guideline: HIG The menu bar: 'Excluding commands from the menu bar risks making them difficult for everyone to find'; View menu; HIG Keyboards: 'Support Full Keyboard Access'.
findings.fix: Anchor the magnification at the gesture's startLocation (adjust offset by the usual (1-ratio)*(anchor-centre) term, still through clampedOffset). Add View menu items Zoom In / Zoom Out / Actual Size on the pane under the pointer or the active pane (ActivePaneOutline already tracks it) that call ZoomPan.step/reset. Correct the header comment.

findings.title: Fit-annulus radii for Fit Ellipse are typed blind; the annulus is never drawn on the pattern
findings.what: 'Fit annulus inner' and 'Fit annulus outer' are two NumericFields (px, defaults 0.35 and 0.9 of the half detector in AppState+Open.swift:523). A grep for ellipseFitInnerRadius finds no use in any overlay (PaneOverlays, ImagePanes, FitOverlays): only the fit result is drawn afterwards (drawEllipse). The Fit Ellipse tooltip says the annulus 'must contain a ring with broad angular coverage', and a refusal for coverage is the failure mode ('Fit Anyway'), yet the user cannot see which ring the numbers select.
findings.guideline: HIG Sliders / Entering data: show the exact value and give live feedback ('live feedback shows people results in real time').
findings.fix: Draw the two circles as thin dashed outlines on the diffraction pane while the Ellipse correction section is expanded (same halo style as ApertureOutline), optionally draggable. Reuse ApertureOutline.metrics so figures and screen agree.

findings.title: Load configurator crop is drag-replace only: no handles, no numeric fields
findings.what: cropPane (in the file LoadConfigurator composes) uses DragGesture(minimumDistance: 8) that recomputes the whole rectangle from the drag start each time; the drawn rectangle has allowsHitTesting(false), so an existing crop cannot be moved or resized, only redrawn. The crop's numbers appear only indirectly in the Size section ('Loaded shape'). Steppers exist only inside the VoiceOver modifier (ScanCropEdit). A 1-pixel-off crop on a large scan means redrawing at preview resolution (the real-space preview is strided, so edges may not be reachable exactly by dragging).
findings.guideline: HIG Sliders ('exact value in a text field'); HIG Keyboards ('Shift constrains', arrow keys move by the smallest unit).
findings.fix: Show the crop as editable rows under each preview (X, Y, width, height in source pixels) bound to LoadConfiguration; keep drag as the quick path. Stays inside the existing sheet; costs about 4 rows in the Form.

findings.title: Refusal in the load sheet colours the whole sentence orange
findings.what: The refusal Text(refusal) uses .font(.caption).foregroundStyle(.orange) with no symbol; the same sheet's other warning (InspectorWarning for memory, line 158) and PreprocessSheet's refusal (InspectorWarning with exclamationmark.triangle, PreprocessSheet.swift ~line 262) already use the symbol-plus-primary-text pattern. Orange caption text on the grouped-form background is also low contrast in Light mode, and the Load button is silently disabled beside it.
findings.guideline: HIG Color: do not rely on colour alone; use system label colours for text. Owner rule (inspector-hig-recipe): colour on status symbols, never whole titles or sentences.
findings.fix: Replace with InspectorWarning(refusal, systemImage: "exclamationmark.triangle") as PreprocessSheet does; keep the identifier.

findings.title: Preprocess sheet colours the whole calibration verdict green/orange
findings.what: Label(verdict.summary, systemImage:) has .foregroundStyle(verdict.quantitative ? Color.green : Color.orange) on the Label, so the sentence turns green or orange. PrepareSettings.swift:182 colours only the symbol and keeps the sentence primary, and CalibrationReadinessRow does the same; the two surfaces show the same verdict differently.
findings.guideline: HIG Color / Labels; owner rule: colour on status symbols only, never coloured text.
findings.fix: Move the tint to the icon (Label with explicit icon closure, as PrepareSettings does) and keep the text primary.

findings.title: Histogram window handles are the same accent colour as the bars they sit on
findings.what: draw() fills bars with Color.accentColor and handleBar() fills the 2 pt handle line and 9 pt knob with Color.accentColor too, so inside the retained window the handle line is invisible against a tall bar; only the dimming of the tails (black 0.4) shows where the window is. The whole-histogram drag moves the nearest handle (lines ~140-150), so the user must infer which handle is nearest.
findings.guideline: HIG Color (sufficient contrast, do not rely on one hue); HIG Sliders (clear thumb).
findings.fix: Draw the handle in a contrasting system colour (.primary line with a small halo, or white/black outline as ApertureOutline does) and keep bars accent. Tier 3, no layout change.

findings.title: No zoom indicator or reset affordance on the diffraction pane
findings.what: RealSpacePane shows a 'Pan x2.0' badge (zoomModeBadge, line ~915) with the reset hint, but DiffractionPane has no badge: after a pinch the pattern is zoomed with nothing in the header saying so, and the only way back is an undiscoverable double-click (ZoomPan.swift:149) or the VoiceOver action. The scale bar is zoom-aware, so it does tell an attentive reader, but a user comparing mean and max patterns can lose track of the 1:1 view.
findings.guideline: HIG Pointing devices / gestures: do not make gestures the only way; HIG The menu bar (commands should be findable).
findings.fix: Show the same small zoom badge (and a 'Reset' help) in the diffraction header when zoom is not 1; resolves together with the View-menu Actual Size item.

findings.title: Pane image border is white at 8% opacity, invisible in Light mode
findings.what: .border(Color.white.opacity(0.08)) frames both panes (also line 1153). On a light window background a white line at 8% is not visible, so a pattern or map with a bright edge (or the transparent region around a rotated map) has no defined edge; ScanNavigatorInset uses white at 0.55 over black, which is fine only because it has its own black background.
findings.guideline: HIG Dark Mode / Color: use semantic colours that adapt, e.g. Color.separator or .quaternary.
findings.fix: Use Color(nsColor: .separatorColor)-equivalent semantic colour (e.g. .separator via ShapeStyle) so the frame reads in both appearances.

findings.title: Preprocess 'Real-space crop' section holds only a stride stepper
findings.what: Section("Real-space crop") contains just Stepper "Scan stride N x"; the crop itself is drawn in the preview panes above. A stride (every Nth position) is thinning, not cropping, and the same word 'crop' is used elsewhere for the rectangle (LoadConfigurator header comment insists crop is distinct from other terms).
findings.guideline: HIG Writing / Labels: name controls for what they do; owner rule: no filler, wording earns its place.
findings.fix: Rename the section 'Scan thinning' (or 'Scan stride') and put the crop hint ('Drag a rectangle on the scan preview') as its caption.

findings.title: Replace-everything actions have no confirmation, while the low-stakes Reset does
findings.what: Import Labels… (line ~590) sets importingLabels and the file importer calls appState.importDiskCentreLabels, whose status line says '(replaced the current labels)': hand-clicked disk centres, the owner's training work, are overwritten on pick with no dialog. Likewise PhaseMappingSettings.swift:444 'Al–Mg–Si (β″ needles)…' replaces the whole phase list (its own help says 'Replaces the phase list') with no dialog, and the PhaseRow minus button (PhaseMappingSettings.swift:525) removes a phase and its typed zone axis, relationship and slab with one click. Yet 'Reset Recommended Settings' (MapSettings.swift:825) does get a confirmationDialog. No UndoManager is used anywhere in UI/App/Session (grep). Protection is inverted: cheap resets are guarded, hand-made data is not.
findings.guideline: HIG 'Undo and redo' (people expect to reverse recent actions; Edit menu Cmd-Z) and HIG 'Alerts' (confirm destructive actions that cannot be undone).
findings.fix: Preferred under the owner's 'simple' rule: make these three register an undo (label 'Import Labels', 'Apply Al–Mg–Si Preset', 'Remove Phase') rather than add dialogs. If undo is too big, a one-line confirmation only for Import Labels when labels exist and for the preset when the list is non-empty. Leave the single-phase minus alone if undo lands.

findings.title: Materials Project sheet: Return fetches again after a successful fetch; Import is never the default
findings.what: Fetch carries .keyboardShortcut(.defaultAction) (line 209) permanently; Import (line 212) has no shortcut. After a fetch succeeds and the card shows the result, Return re-fetches rather than importing, so the flow is type id, Return, click Import with the mouse. The mp-id field also has no @FocusState, so the sheet opens with nothing focused and the user must click the field first (no focus declaration anywhere in the file).
findings.guideline: HIG 'Sheets' / 'Buttons' (the default button is the likely next action; Return triggers it) and HIG 'Keyboards' / 'Focus and selection' (initial focus on the first field).
findings.fix: Make the default action Fetch while outcome is nil or a failure, and Import once canImport(outcome:) is true (swap the modifier by state); give mp-id @FocusState initial focus with .onSubmit { fetch }.

findings.title: Status carried by coloured words, not symbols, in the phase-mapping and disk rooms
findings.what: The owner's inspector recipe says colour goes on status symbols and text stays in system label colours. Still orange/red whole text: zone-axis rows 'at chance' / 'no better than a wrong axis' (lines 125-128), the two caption2 paragraphs 'No axis beats chance…' / 'No axis stands out…' (141-142, 149-150), the 'On this detector' value (264), the 'Orientations' count (162), the exploratory-scale Label (400-404), and in MapSettings.swift: validation issue Labels (~460, whole Label red/orange), 'Exploratory scale' note (1405), DetectionSettingsStaleWarning (1486) and the zone-axis malformed captions (PhaseMappingSettings 545, 557). InspectorWarning itself (InspectorRows.swift:593-597) applies .orange to the whole Label, so every caller inherits it. The caveats that matter most scientifically sit in caption2 (about 10 pt) orange.
findings.guideline: HIG 'Color' (do not rely on colour alone; use system colours with meaning) and HIG 'Typography' (avoid very small text); the owner's inspector-hig-recipe note says this explicitly.
findings.fix: Change InspectorWarning to tint only the symbol (.symbolRenderingMode/.foregroundStyle on the icon, text .secondary or .primary) and use it for the listed rows; give the zone-axis verdict an InspectorStatusRow-style triangle on the symbol; use .caption not .caption2 for the 'undecided' paragraphs.

findings.title: Object table: numeric columns left-aligned, export loses context and swallows errors
findings.what: Area, Length, Width, Aspect, Orientation cells are plain Text(...).monospacedDigit() in leading-aligned cells, so mixed-magnitude decimals (3 significant digits, e.g. 4,82 vs 123) do not line up and are hard to scan. The toolbar Export CSV uses defaultFilename 'precipitate-objects.csv' (line 88) while the inspector section names it after the dataset (PrecipitateObjectsSection.swift:176), and the completion is '{ _ in }' (line 89) so a write failure is silent (the section version reports it in statusText). Beside the Phase/Counted-only filters, the button exports every row regardless of the filter, which the tooltip says but the placement implies otherwise. The Position column is sorted by centroidY only (line 182).
findings.guideline: HIG 'Lists and tables' (descriptive headings, sortable and resizable columns; macOS tables are for scanning columns of values); HIG 'Alerts'/'Feedback' (report failures).
findings.fix: Right-align numeric cells (.frame(maxWidth: .infinity, alignment: .trailing)); build the filename from the report's source name; handle .failure by showing an alert or the status line; consider adding a Copy command on the selected rows (tab-separated, units in header) since this table feeds figures and spreadsheets.

findings.title: Steppers carry ranges too large for step-by-one
findings.what: Maximum peaks is a Stepper over 1...500 (line 682) with the value shown only as label text; Min. peak spacing and Reference minimum radius step by 1 over 0...detector size (lines 737-800); ACOM Center X / Center Y step 1 over 0...(scan size-1) (lines 1083-1105); Half-size 4...min(rx,ry)/2. Moving from 70 to 200 peaks, or Center X from 12 to 240, is hundreds of clicks, and SwiftUI's Stepper gives no Shift-click multiplier. The five/ten other fields in the same sections (Min. intensity, Threshold) already use NumericField, so the inspector mixes both idioms.
findings.guideline: HIG 'Steppers': 'Consider pairing a stepper with a text field when large value changes are likely'; on macOS consider Shift-click for larger steps.
findings.fix: Use NumericField (typed, clamped to the range) for Maximum peaks, spacing, radius and Center X/Y, keeping a Stepper only for the small-range ones (Reference peak rank, Upsample). Center X/Y are also settable by clicking the scan pane, so the typed field is enough.

findings.title: Learned-detector threshold is a typed number; Detector picker shows one choice when learned is hidden
findings.what: The Threshold row (lines 336-343) is a NumericField for a bounded 0.3-0.99 pick level that changes the preview live (onChange re-runs detectCurrentPattern, line 340), i.e. a value explored interactively; other 0-1 quantities in the Advanced section use AdjustmentSlider. Separately, with 'Offer the learned detector' off (AppPreferences.offerLearnedDetector, default true), offeredDetectorClasses is [.classical] and the Detector row (lines 322-338) is still a Picker with exactly one item and a tooltip about the neural net.
findings.guideline: HIG 'Sliders' (approximate value within a bounded range, immediate feedback) and HIG 'Pop-up buttons'/'Pickers' (a control with a single option is not a choice); owner rule 'every control earns its place'.
findings.fix: Use AdjustmentSlider with the typed field for Threshold (as the Advanced section does); hide the Detector row when offeredDetectorClasses.count == 1.

findings.title: Decimal formatting is not locale-aware in the phase and Materials Project readouts
findings.what: Results are printed with String(format:) (phase fractions '%.1f %%' line 332, zone-axis fit '%.0f %% · %.4f Å⁻¹' line 120, chance match '%.1f %%' ~391, matrix in-plane '%.0f°' ~396, ring hint in MapSettings ~234, cell 'a=%.4g' in MaterialsProjectImportSheet.swift:164-167), while the neighbouring fields and PrecipitateFormat use locale-aware FormatStyle (the 2026-10-08 P2a/V-F1 lane fixed only some). In a German region the Precipitates rows read '23,1 nm' and the phase fraction right above reads '12.3 %', and the typed fields in the same inspector use the comma.
findings.guideline: HIG 'Right to left'/'Internationalization' guidance and Foundation FormatStyle (numbers in the person's locale); the 2026-10-07 review's own FormatStyle swap set the standard.

findings.title: No pointer feedback when drawing, moving or resizing a region

Plain two-finger scroll does not pan the spectrum, and the code documents that as a pure-SwiftUI choice (ZoomPan.swift); I did not list it as a finding because it is an existing owner decision, but it is the first thing a Mac user will try. (7) The meaning of the Maps/Smooth/Auto ID row order and the inspector's total height (CLAUDE.md asks to cost a UI change in rows or points). I did not read the whole of SpectroscopyLogic.swift, SpectroscopyRoomModel.swift, QuantifyPresentation.swift, MapRasters.swift or the controller's compute paths, only their on-screen strings and the parts the views call. I did not re-check items the 2026-10-07 review and the 2026-10-08/13 accessibility lanes fixed (rotor, VoiceOver actions, FormatStyle swaps in readouts, focus strokes, tile label stability). Apple docs were read for Offering help, File management, Pointing devices, Accessibility, Segmented controls and Context menus. The menu-bar and Color pages were cited from the search listing and the context-menus text, not read in full.

findings.title: Warnings and caveats are coloured text (orange/red/green), often 10 pt with no symbol
findings.what: InspectorWarning (584-597) draws the whole Label in .font(.caption) + .foregroundStyle(.orange), 19 call sites. 28 further hand-rolled sites colour the text itself: PhaseMappingSettings.swift:125,127 ('at chance', 'no better than a wrong axis'), :142,:150 (caption2 paragraphs ending 'Treat the ranking as undecided'), :545,:557 (caption2); MapSettings.swift:1405,1486 (caption), :1373 ('Interpretation' value coloured green/orange); ReconstructionSettings.swift:77,85,121,734; LoadConfigurator.swift:179; MaterialsProjectImportSheet.swift:195 (a '⚠' character in the string); ImagePanes.swift:117 ('ROI sum' badge). Most have no symbol. PrepareSettings.swift:178-186 already does it right ('Colour on the symbol only; the sentence stays primary text').
findings.guideline: HIG Color: 'Avoid relying solely on color ... communicate essential information'; HIG Accessibility: text up to 17 pt needs 4.5:1 contrast. System orange is about (255,141,40) in light mode, roughly 2.3:1 on white (my calculation). Also the owner's inspector-hig-recipe: colour on status symbols, never whole green/orange titles.
findings.fix: Make InspectorWarning draw the symbol in orange and the text in .primary or .secondary, then route the hand-rolled orange Text sites through it (add a symbol where there is none). Use .callout or .subheadline for the long ranking caveats rather than caption2. Keep the PrepareSettings pattern as the model. Colour the 'Interpretation' value with a leading seal/triangle symbol, text in label colour.

findings.title: Scientific honesty disclosures use 10 pt tertiary text
findings.what: 'Real-space and max previews are sampled. The single-position pattern is exact.' is .font(.caption2).foregroundStyle(.tertiary) (ReductionSections.swift:158-160). 'Not a result — cannot be exported or saved.' is the same style at WorkspaceInspector.swift:411-413 (frozen file). The rotation-plot explanation 'solid: as-is, dashed: transposed. The marker is the minimum the fit found; it was not written.' is caption2 tertiary at WorkspaceInspector.swift:883,886. Tertiary label colour is a low-alpha grey; at the HIG's 10 pt minimum it will not reach 4.5:1.
findings.guideline: HIG Typography: macOS default 13 pt, minimum 10 pt; HIG Accessibility: 4.5:1 minimum contrast for text up to 17 pt. The repo rule 'Unvalidated stays labelled' also favours legible caveats.
findings.fix: Show caveats that change how a number or image is read in .secondary at .subheadline or .callout (InspectorNote at a larger size). Keep .tertiary only for decorative axis tick labels. In WorkspaceInspector.swift this is a style change, so it needs an owner-accepted picture first.

findings.title: Bare Buttons inside InspectorActionRow do not match the glass adaptive buttons and can truncate
findings.what: 46 inspector actions use InspectorAdaptiveButton (.buttonStyle(.glass), icon-only fallback so nothing truncates). Eight actions are bare Button(...) inside InspectorActionRow and take the automatic bordered style with a fixed text label: Prepare's calibration actions ('Fit Detector Ellipse', 'Measure R–Q Rotation', 'Calibrate from Selected Material', origin action; CalibrationReadinessRow.swift:181,189,197,206), 'Export Figure…' (FigureExportSection.swift:59), the EDX 'Results CSV…', 'Spectrum CSV…' (SpectroscopyInspectors.swift:458,489) and Auto ID 'Cancel' (:87). The InspectorRows header comment still says 'plain bordered push button' while InspectorAdaptiveButton says glass (owner 2026-10-07). Prepare is the reference room and these sit next to glass buttons. This is read from the code only; I did not see it on screen.
findings.guideline: HIG Buttons: 'Use style — not size' and buttons in a set should match; owner standard: 'buttons never tiny or truncated'.
findings.fix: Apply .buttonStyle(.glass) inside InspectorActionRow, or convert the eight sites to InspectorAdaptiveButton with a symbol (e.g. square.and.arrow.up for the exports). Update the stale kit comment.

findings.title: Image zoom and pan exist only as trackpad gestures, double-click and VoiceOver actions
findings.what: Zoom is a MagnifyGesture plus drag and double-click reset (ZoomPan.swift:101-150); the same in ResultsWorkspace.swift:457. The only non-gesture path is the VoiceOver action list (:178-190). The command menus in App/mac4DSTEMApp.swift:143-290 have no Zoom In, Zoom Out or Actual Size, and nothing handles the scroll wheel. The file header says macOS synthesises magnification from a mouse wheel with a modifier; I could not confirm this (it looks like the system Zoom accessibility feature). The EDX spectrum already supports + = − keys, so the image panes are the odd ones out.
findings.guideline: HIG Accessibility: 'Offer alternatives to gestures' and 'Let people use the keyboard alone'.
findings.fix: Add View-menu Zoom In (⌘+), Zoom Out (⌘−), Actual Size (⌘0) acting on the focused pane, reusing ZoomPan.step/reset. Optionally ⌥-scroll to zoom. Verify or correct the mouse-wheel claim in the comment.

findings.title: AdjustmentSlider reset is hidden behind a double-click on the label
findings.what: The reset is Text(label).onTapGesture(count: 2) with the tooltip 'Double-click to reset' (416-424), shown only when a defaultValue exists. The label is not focusable and nothing is drawn when the value differs from the default. Keyboard-only and mouse-only users who never hover the label have no path; VoiceOver has the 'Reset to default' action (:410). Used for Gamma in the display popover (PaneOverlays.swift:457,471) and the EDX map gamma (MapsGridView.swift:600).
findings.guideline: HIG Accessibility: keyboard alone, and alternatives to gestures; owner reference Pixelmator Pro: a reset control in the row's title.
findings.fix: When defaultValue != nil and the value differs, show a borderless arrow.counterclockwise button (help 'Reset to default') at the trailing end of the label row. Keep the double-click as a shortcut.

findings.title: Periodic table is 90+ separate Tab stops with no arrow-key navigation
findings.what: Every cell is its own plain Button; the comment says 'the 90+ tab stops are accepted' (:129). There is no .focusSection(), onMoveCommand or arrow-key handling. A keyboard user must Tab through up to 90 cells to reach a late element, and then through the rest to leave the section. The hand-built 'Lanthanides and actinides' fold (:92-105) also repeats the section-header chevron and tooltip by hand rather than using the kit.
findings.guideline: HIG Accessibility: 'Let people use the keyboard alone to navigate'; HIG Keyboards (arrow keys move within a group); SwiftUI focusSection / onMoveCommand.
findings.fix: Treat the grid as one focus group: Tab enters once, arrow keys move between cells (a roving focus with onMoveCommand), Space toggles, Tab leaves. Keep the VoiceOver actions and rotor.

findings.title: Glass chip groups show the on-state by tint alone and are not announced as a group
findings.what: ChipButton is plain-styled text at a fixed .font(.system(size: 12)) (:1026). The on-state is only .tint(accent or the chip's colour at 55 % opacity) on .glassEffect (:1032); there is no checkmark or weight change. The group is .accessibilityElement(.contain) with .isSelected on each chip (:1036) but no picker or radio semantics. Used as a picker for EDX map mode, region tools, curve and overlay toggles (SpectroscopyInspectors.swift:66,174,352-358). The fixed 12 pt is below the owner's 13 pt inspector rule. Glass here is the controls layer, not content, and is already justified by Apple's custom-view guidance cited in the code. Caveat: the owner liked Liquid Glass buttons (2026-10-07); I found no record that he accepted the chips.
findings.guideline: HIG Toggles: 'Avoid relying solely on different colors to communicate state'; HIG Color: more than colour alone; HIG Typography: macOS default 13 pt.
findings.fix: Add a non-colour cue to the on chip (leading checkmark or semibold title). Use 13 pt (.body). Give single-mode groups picker or radio semantics for VoiceOver and arrow-key movement.

findings.title: Inspector section disclosure ignores Reduce Motion
findings.what: InspectorSectionBody.header toggles with withAnimation(.easeInOut(duration: 0.15)) and rotates the chevron (:163-170) without reading accessibilityReduceMotion. Every other animation in the app does read it: PeriodicTableView.swift:95, MapsGridView.swift:63/638, ZoomPan.swift:159-166. This one is the most-used animation in the app, on every section of every room.
findings.guideline: HIG Accessibility: when Reduce Motion is on, reduce automatic and repetitive animation and replace movement with fades.
findings.fix: Add @Environment(\.accessibilityReduceMotion) and use withAnimation(reduceMotion ? nil : ...), as the periodic-table fold does.

findings.title: Type scale: 124 caption/caption2 uses, both exactly 10 pt, and a few sizes below the HIG minimum
findings.what: InspectorNote (all explanatory prose, 63 uses) and InspectorWarning use .font(.caption), which is 10 pt on macOS, the HIG minimum. There are 97 .caption and 27 .caption2 uses in UI/. Caption 1 and Caption 2 are the same 10 pt (caption2 only adds Medium weight), so the two names give no real hierarchy. The owner rule is 13-pt text in the inspector, small only in the strip. Below the 10 pt minimum: the periodic-table symbol is sized by cell and allows minimumScaleFactor 0.8, which the code comment places at 9 pt in the narrowest cell, so about 7 pt (PeriodicTableView.swift:135-136); the 'SCAN' inset label is 9 pt (ImagePanes.swift:615-618).
findings.guideline: HIG Typography: macOS built-in text styles (Footnote and Caption 1/2 are 10 pt) and 'Follow the recommended default and minimum text sizes' (default 13, minimum 10).
findings.fix: Make InspectorNote .subheadline (11 pt) or .callout (12 pt) and fold caption2 into one style. Floor the periodic-table symbol at 10 pt (a taller minimum cell, or a smaller abbreviation only when needed) and SCAN at 10 pt. Cost it in rows and points first: it changes inspector height and the width-budget tests.

findings.title: Toggle style differs inside the same popover and inspector
findings.what: The display popover holds 'Log y-axis' (HistogramView.swift:48-52: .switch, .controlSize(.small)) and 'Log display' (PaneOverlays.swift:506: default style, a checkbox in a Form). The pane header toggles 'Fit overlay' and 'Show claimed disks' are small switches (ImagePanes.swift:185-195). Reconstruction, Map and Spectroscopy inspector toggles are checkboxes with the label at the leading edge (e.g. ReconstructionSettings.swift:243-280, FigureExportSection.swift:37). Two adjacent 'Log ...' toggles mean different things (axis versus image) and look different.
findings.guideline: HIG Toggles (macOS): 'In general, don't replace a checkbox with a switch'; a mini switch is for a row in a grouped form. Conflict: HIG says a checkbox's title sits on its trailing side, but the owner's Pixelmator alignment rule (label leading, control trailing) wins, so keep that.
findings.fix: Choose one style for on/off rows in popovers and inspectors (checkbox, matching the majority) and keep switches only where one switch governs a group. Rename the two 'Log' toggles to 'Log intensity (image)' and 'Log counts (histogram)'.

findings.title: Buttons that go to another room use four wordings and four icons; the menu says 'Go to'
findings.what: Room-navigation buttons read 'Go to Bragg Disks' (circle.grid.cross, MapSettings.swift:984), 'Open Prepare' (wrench.and.screwdriver, WorkspaceInspector.swift:249), 'Improve in Prepare' (same icon, WorkspaceInspector.swift:281), 'Open Prepare to Calibrate' (arrow.right.circle, ReconstructionSettings.swift:96) and 'Review Q Calibration in Prepare' (checkmark.seal, MapSettings.swift:1387). The Workspace menu says 'Go to <Room>' (mac4DSTEMApp.swift:289).
findings.guideline: HIG Buttons / Writing: label a button with a verb that says what it does, and use one wording and symbol for the same action across the app.
findings.fix: Use one verb and one symbol for 'jump to a room' (e.g. 'Go to Prepare' with arrow.right.circle) and keep the reason in the hint or help. This is a wording change.

findings.title: EDX Thickness uncertainty row is labelled only 'σ'
findings.what: InspectorRow("σ") holds the thickness uncertainty field, directly under the 'Thickness' row, and only appears once a thickness is set. The field's accessibility title is 'Thickness σ' (:409) so VoiceOver is fine, but a sighted reader sees a bare Greek letter beside a nm field, with no indent or caption to say whose σ it is (the Absorption note sits above).
findings.guideline: HIG Labels: use clear, concise labels that describe the control without relying on context; owner: 'every control earns its place', with an intuitive UI.
findings.fix: Label the row 'Thickness σ', or indent it under Thickness with the same title.

notChecked: Not assessed, since I could not see the app (read-only, nothing launched): the real rendered contrast of orange, tertiary and tinted-chip text in light and dark mode and with Increase Contrast; how the glass-button versus bordered-button mismatch actually looks; the inspector width budget and row heights after the type-size change (the cost in rows and points the repo requires); the real size of the periodic-table cells at the narrowest inspector width; how Full Keyboard Access and VoiceOver actually behave on the chip groups, the periodic table and the slider reset; Reduce Transparency behaviour of the glass chips; the Xcode and Pixelmator reference apps themselves; and the printed or exported figure typography. I looked up the HIG pages Color, Toggles, Accessibility and Typography through the Apple docs server. I did not separately look up the Sliders, Menus, Keyboards, Inspectors, Materials, Buttons or SF Symbols pages, so findings on those topics rest on the Accessibility page, the owner's memory notes (which cite Buttons and Materials) and the code.
